content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium severity) — redline proposed and validated.**

**What I checked:**
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — mutual confidentiality obligations only; no return-or-destroy mechanic on termination.
- **§ 13 (Term)** — actually cuts *against* us: it makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, with no corresponding TrueLink duty to help or hand back data.
- **§ 14 (Termination)** — sets only the date services cease.
- **§ 2(f) (Backups)** — governs TrueLink's internal backup practice, not Client access or export.
- Searches for "termination", "return", and "data" surfaced no transition, exit, export, or deletion language anywhere in the document.

**Why it's a deviation, not a fallback:** the agreement doesn't reach even the fallback position (90 days' assistance + export within 30 days). This is a hosting agreement holding borrower and loan data — including Credit Data, which § 10(c) deems Client Proprietary Information — so on exit we would have migration deadlines but no contractual right to our own data in usable form.

**Redline (inserted after § 14, preferred position):** TrueLink to (a) provide up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates on request; (b) return all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days; and (c) thereafter delete and certify deletion in writing, with a carve-out for legally required retention (sensible given the regulated credit data). Placement is deliberate: § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination, so the new paragraph survives without needing a separate survival hook.

The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an available fallback if TrueLink pushes back on the six-month tail.
